record.paper_title: Massive Stars: Some Open Questions and the role of Multi-Object Spectroscopy
record.original_question: What is the physical origin of macroturbulent line broadening in massive O and B stars? The paper states that this broadening mechanism is real but of unknown origin, that the commonly suggested explanation in terms of kappa-driven gravity-mode pulsations does not explain many high-mass stars, and that alternative ideas involving turbulent pressure from subsurface convection or convection-driven internal gravity waves remain under investigation. The unresolved issue is whether one of these mechanisms dominates or whether several processes contribute in different parts of parameter space.

evidence.quote: Besides the well known mechanisms that we find in textbooks (like the natural, Doppler or the different collisional broadening mechanisms) spectral lines in massive O and B stars are affected by a brodening mechanism of still unknown origin. It is usually called macroturbulence
Thus this kind of pulsations do not seem to explain the presence of macroturbulent broadening in high-mass stars

Recently, Grassitelli et al. (2015) propose that turbulent pressure, originated by sub-surface convective layers, may be at the root of this extra broadening and Aerts & Rogers (2015) conclude that it may be explained by convection-driven internal gravity waves (IGW)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Spectral lines observed in massive O- and B-type stars exhibit a non-thermal broadening component, conventionally called macroturbulent broadening, which is in excess of thermal Doppler broadening, natural broadening, collisional broadening, and rotational broadening, and which is empirically modeled by convolving the intrinsic line profile with a (typically radial-tangential) velocity distribution of characteristic amplitude of order tens of km/s. The physical mechanism producing this broadening is not established. Candidate mechanisms include: (i) collective effects of high-order, low-degree heat-driven (kappa-mechanism) gravity-mode pulsations excited in the stellar envelope; (ii) turbulent pressure fluctuations generated by subsurface convective layers associated with the iron opacity bump; and (iii) coherent and stochastic surface velocity fields produced by convection-driven internal gravity waves propagating from the convective core (or from subsurface convection zones) to the photosphere.

Determine the physical origin of macroturbulent line broadening in massive O- and B-type stars across the Hertzsprung–Russell diagram. Specifically, decide whether a single mechanism among (i)–(iii) is dominant throughout the OB regime, or whether different mechanisms dominate in distinct regions of the parameter space spanned by mass, evolutionary stage, and surface gravity; and in the latter case, identify the boundaries in this parameter space and the relative contributions of each mechanism to the observed macroturbulent velocity.
artifact.category_tag: Stellar astrophysics — line broadening in massive stars
artifact.status_search_result: Recent observational and modeling work (notably the 2024 A&A study from the ESO UVES/FEROS Large Programs of TESS OB pulsators) provides evidence that kappa-driven gravity-mode pulsations alone cannot explain macroturbulence in high-mass stars, that subsurface iron-opacity-bump convection (FeCZ) correlates with macroturbulent velocities for stars above ~30 M⊙, and that internal gravity waves are favored for stars below ~12 M⊙, with both contributing in the intermediate range. The problem is therefore partially resolved: a regime-dependent picture is emerging, but a definitive, quantitative attribution across all OB stars remains open.

status_evidence.title: The ESO UVES/FEROS Large Programs of TESS OB pulsators – II. The physical origin of macroturbulence
status_evidence.snippet: Stars with initial masses above 30 M⊙ exhibit macroturbulent velocities in line with FeCZ properties; for stars below 12 M⊙ alternative mechanisms such as IGWs are needed; in the 12–30 M⊙ range both can contribute.
status_evidence.claim: Different mechanisms dominate in different mass regimes, indicating partial resolution.

status_evidence.title: The IACOB project. III. New observational clues to understand macroturbulent broadening in massive O- and B-type stars
status_evidence.snippet: Provides observational clues constraining candidate mechanisms but does not uniquely identify the origin.
status_evidence.claim: The origin of macroturbulence remained unresolved as of 2017, with multiple candidates still considered.

status_evidence.title: Observational evidence for a correlation between macroturbulent broadening and line-profile variations in OB supergiants
status_evidence.snippet: Correlation suggests stellar oscillations contribute to macroturbulent broadening in OB supergiants.
